title: Dimensionality Reduction Quiz
description: Test your understanding of dimensionality reduction techniques and their applications

questions.text: What is the primary goal of dimensionality reduction?
options: To increase the number of features in the dataset
To reduce the number of features while preserving important information
To convert categorical features to numerical features
To remove outliers from the dataset
questions.explanation: Dimensionality reduction aims to reduce the number of features (dimensions) in a dataset while preserving as much important information as possible, helping to combat the curse of dimensionality and improve computational efficiency.

questions.text: Which dimensionality reduction technique finds directions of maximum variance in the data?
options: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)
Independent Component Analysis (ICA)
Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
questions.explanation: PCA finds orthogonal directions (principal components) that capture the maximum variance in the data. It projects the data onto these directions to reduce dimensionality while preserving as much variance as possible.

questions.text: LDA requires labeled data because it optimizes for class separation.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: True. LDA is a supervised dimensionality reduction technique that requires labeled data because it finds directions that maximize the separation between different classes while minimizing within-class variance.

options: The difficulty of visualizing high-dimensional data
The phenomenon where data becomes sparse and distances become similar in high dimensions
The increased computational cost of processing many features
All of the above
questions.explanation: The curse of dimensionality encompasses all these issues: data sparsity, distance concentration, computational complexity, visualization challenges, and increased risk of overfitting in high-dimensional spaces.

questions.text: Which method is best suited for the 'cocktail party problem' of separating mixed audio signals?
options: PCA
LDA
ICA
SVD
questions.explanation: ICA (Independent Component Analysis) is specifically designed for blind source separation problems like the cocktail party problem, where the goal is to separate mixed signals into their independent source components.

questions.text: In PCA, what do the eigenvalues represent?
options: The direction of the principal components
The amount of variance explained by each principal component
The correlation between features
The number of components to keep
questions.explanation: In PCA, eigenvalues represent the amount of variance explained by each corresponding principal component (eigenvector). Larger eigenvalues indicate components that capture more variance in the data.

questions.text: What is a 'scree plot' used for in dimensionality reduction?
options: To visualize the reduced-dimensional data
To determine the optimal number of components to keep
To show the correlation between original features
To display the principal component loadings
questions.explanation: A scree plot shows the explained variance (eigenvalues) for each component. It helps determine the optimal number of components by looking for the 'elbow' where the explained variance starts to level off.

questions.text: Which statement about LDA vs PCA is correct?
options: LDA maximizes variance, PCA maximizes class separation
PCA maximizes variance, LDA maximizes class separation
Both methods maximize variance
Both methods maximize class separation
questions.explanation: PCA maximizes variance in the data without considering class labels, while LDA maximizes the separation between classes while minimizing within-class variance. This makes LDA better for classification tasks when labels are available.

questions.text: Why is feature scaling important before applying PCA?
options: PCA doesn't work with unscaled features
Features with larger scales can dominate the principal components
Scaling improves the computational efficiency of PCA
Scaling is not necessary for PCA
questions.explanation: PCA is sensitive to the scale of features because it finds directions of maximum variance. Features with larger scales (e.g., income vs age) will dominate the principal components unless the data is properly scaled first.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of meaningful components that LDA can produce?
options: Equal to the number of original features
Equal to the number of samples
Equal to the number of classes minus one
Unlimited
questions.explanation: LDA can produce at most C-1 meaningful components, where C is the number of classes. This is because LDA finds directions that separate classes, and you need at most C-1 hyperplanes to separate C classes in the optimal way.
